issues.description: The solution repository's Person class declares the field as 'forename' but the rest of the code (getters, setters, equals/hashCode, tests, and the template) use 'firstName'. This name mismatch is a structural error that will cause compilation failures and confusing behavior for students trying to follow the template and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field name consistent with the getters/setters and the template/tests. Rename the field 'forename' in solution_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java to 'firstName' (or alternatively update all getters/setters and usages to 'forename') so that the field name matches across the model, service, resource, and tests.

issues.description: The template and tests consistently use the field name 'firstName' for the Person entity, but the solution repository's Person class declares the attribute as 'forename' while its methods (getFirstName/setFirstName/equals/hashCode) and the rest of the code still reference 'firstName'. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual attribute (the person's first name) across template/tests and solution creates confusion for students mapping requirements to code and will break expectations when students compare or run tests against the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier for the person's given name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the field 'forename' in solution_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java to 'firstName' (and keep existing getters/setters/equals/hashCode), or (B) consistently rename getters/setters/equals/hashCode and all usages in template/tests to use 'forename'. Preferred: rename 'forename' -> 'firstName' in the solution to align with the template and tests.
